sources.finding: Constructor builds numbered shards from supplied count without a persisted topology record.
Get routes hash(key) modulo constructor shard count.
FanoutCache transact exists and enters each shard transaction through ExitStack.
Documents sharding and size limits. Its assertion that FanoutCache lacks transactions conflicts with inspected current source and was not used as a feature-gap claim.
Core stores absolute expiry, tag and raw/serialized or file-backed values; migration must preserve these semantics.
Search surfaced an alternative FanoutCache implementation; no full restartable resharding contract was identified in the reviewed API.

original_contribution: Opt-in durable fanout topology with bounded online source copying and transactional dirty-key reconciliation, atomic publication, progress replay, token/epoch fencing, persistent pause/resume/abort, legacy adoption and independent retired-generation collection. This extends the initial research proposal to allow actual CRUD throughout pending migration.

public_solution_overlap.assessment: Existing FanoutCache sharding and transact are prior art. No matching complete online reshard contract found in bounded pinned-source, official-documentation, issue, and web searches. Several expanded searches were rate limited; this is not a universal absence claim. Hosted tutorial transaction limitations are stale, and the task uses current source instead.

validation.harbor_oracle_nop: Parent owns separate fresh-verifier Harbor integration; fresh direct Docker oracle and baseline completed.

horizon.basis: Interacting online mutation tracking, SQLite/file-payload commits, metadata publication recovery, multi-process coordination, stale topology refresh, bounded progress and compatibility across legacy and current layouts. Not inferred from code length.
horizon.counterevidence: Durable filesystem tasks can score highly in other harnesses; FrontierSWE flash-filesystem Fable5 0.9709 and Fable5.1 0.7779 in a 20-hour harness are parent-recorded counterevidence, not measurements of this task.

limitations: Linux/POSIX local filesystem coordination; unmanaged direct access to managed shard internals is excluded.
Process-crash recovery, not device/power-loss or network-filesystem guarantees.
Native FanoutCache transact is retained; no stronger crash-atomic commit across independent SQLite databases or exactly-once external side effects.
Managed mode supports Disk and JSONDisk and immutable constructor settings; ordinary FanoutCache remains unchanged.
Nonblocking root contention is surfaced as ReshardBusyError and requires caller retry.
Entry work is bounded per step; bytes, directory traversal, initial empty shard creation, explicit abort/collect cleanup, and wall time are not bounded by max_items.
Continuous source mutations may delay quiescent completion.

changes: Removed module-specific time mocking at epoch 1000. TTL tests now use real deadlines several hours in the future/past and compare exact stored deadlines before and after migration. They verify touch, explicit expiry and invisibility of expired entries without a sleep or a patched clock.
Mutation tests reserve an unfinished entry so implementations can cut over eagerly on the last budgeted entry. A valid eager-cutover variant passes the entire suite.

Removed barriers tied to private migration.copied storage and to builtins.open(...).write. Process interruption uses mandatory topology publication boundaries and a public bounded-step acknowledgement barrier. Direct abort-to-idle is accepted without requiring an intermediate aborting phase.

The partial-file recovery requirement remains unchanged. Current tests do not claim to inject a mid-payload failure for every legal copy mechanism; historical reference-only partial-write evidence remains in the initial construction logs.
Corrected the capacity-preservation fixture to make the destination per-shard limit smaller than a copied payload, so an erroneous copy-time cull is observable.
No golden source or public scope changed. The current feature suite has 34 new-feature cases plus 11 compatibility cases.
